slot.brief: Show a plot of log[A] vs t (or ln[A] vs t) for a first-order reaction in a figure; ask what the slope equals (–k/2.303 or –k) or extract k from the slope.

stem: For a first-order reaction, a plot of $\log[A]$ against time is shown in the figure. Find the rate constant $k$.

verdicts.working: The slope is (0 − 1)/(10 − 0) = −0.1 min⁻¹. For a base-10 log plot of a first-order reaction, slope = −k/2.303, so k = 0.2303 min⁻¹.

Independent check: The slope is (0 − 1)/(10 − 0) = −0.1 min⁻¹. For a base-10 log plot of a first-order reaction, slope = −k/2.303, so k = 0.2303 min⁻¹.
solution:
For a first-order reaction, the slope of a plot of $\log[A]$ against time is $-k/2.303$.
$$\text{Slope} = \frac{0-1}{10-0}=-0.100\ \text{min}^{-1},\qquad k=2.303(0.100)=0.2303\ \text{min}^{-1}$$
